name: Bangladesh
snapshot: The February 2026 election, the first since the student uprising that toppled Sheikh Hasina, gave Tarique Rahman's BNP a landslide and ended Muhammad Yunus's interim rule.
culture: Bangladesh was born from the Bengali language movement: on 21 February 1952 students died defending Bangla against Urdu, a day now marked worldwide as International Mother Language Day. Rabindranath Tagore wrote its national anthem. Pohela Boishakh, the Bengali new year, is a huge secular festival, and Dhaka's rickshaw art is a vivid folk tradition.
society: Bangladesh is the world's second-largest garment exporter, and millions of women work in its factories. Microcredit and NGOs helped cut poverty sharply. It is one of the most densely populated countries on Earth and among the most exposed to floods, cyclones and sea-level rise. It hosts about a million Rohingya refugees from Myanmar.

story: For three decades, Bangladesh's politics was a feud between two women: Sheikh Hasina, daughter of the country's founding father, and Khaleda Zia, widow of the general who ruled after him. They took turns in power and took turns jailing each other's people. In August 2024, student-led protests that left hundreds dead toppled Hasina, who fled by helicopter to India. In 2026, Bangladesh held its first election since, and the winner was Khaleda Zia's son.

On 12 February, Tarique Rahman's Bangladesh Nationalist Party won a landslide, and he was sworn in as prime minister on 17 February, taking over from Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus, who had led an interim government for 18 months (People Daily). Rahman, 60, had returned only in December after 17 years of exile in Britain, fleeing multiple convictions under Hasina, including a life sentence, that his supporters called political (CIDOB). Hasina's Awami League was barred from running, and Hasina herself has been sentenced to death in absentia for crimes against humanity over the crackdown on the protests. The Islamist Jamaat-e-Islami, crushed under Hasina, made big gains and conceded as the main opposition. Rahman has promised to end disappearances and extrajudicial killings, but Human Rights Watch notes the notorious Rapid Action Battalion survives under a new name, mob violence has surged and attacks on Hindus and other minorities continue (HRW). The deeper question for 170 million Bangladeshis is whether the revolution of 2024 ends the old feud or just hands it to the next generation.
briefing.power: A parliamentary republic. The prime minister leads the majority in the 350-seat Jatiya Sangsad (300 directly elected, 50 reserved for women); the president, elected by parliament, is largely ceremonial.
briefing.holders: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman (BNP), in office since 17 February 2026.
